questions.stem: If the image of the point $(-4, 5)$ in the line $x + 2y = 2$ lies on the circle $(x + 4)^{2} + (y - 3)^{2} = r^{2}$, then $r$ is equal to :

Let $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 5\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c} = 3\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \lambda\hat{k}$ be three vectors. Let $\vec{r}$ be a unit vector along $\vec{b} + \vec{c}$. If $\vec{r} \cdot \vec{a} = 3$, then $3\lambda$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\vec{r} = k(\vec{b} + \vec{c})$
$\vec{r} \cdot \vec{a} = 3$
$\vec{r} \cdot \vec{a} = k(\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a})$
$3 = k(2 + 6 - 15 + 3 - 2 + 3\lambda)$
$3 = k(-6 + 3\lambda)$ $\quad$ ...(1)
$\vec{r} = k(5\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - (5 - \lambda)\hat{k})$
$|\vec{r}| = k\sqrt{25 + 4 + 25 + \lambda^{2} - 10\lambda} = 1$ $\quad$ ...(2)
$k = \frac{3}{-6 + 3\lambda} = \frac{1}{-2 + \lambda}$ $\quad$ put in (2)
$4 + \lambda^{2} - 4\lambda = 54 + \lambda^{2} - 10\lambda$
$6\lambda = 50$
$3\lambda = 25$

questions.stem: The sum of all possible values of $\theta \in [-\pi, 2\pi]$, for which $\frac{1 + i\cos\theta}{1 - 2i\cos\theta}$ is purely imaginary, is equal to
questions.solution:
$Z = \frac{1 + i\cos\theta}{1 - 2i\cos\theta}$
$Z = -\bar{Z} \Rightarrow \frac{1 + i\cos\theta}{1 - 2i\cos\theta} = -\left(\overline{\frac{1 + i\cos\theta}{1 - 2i\cos\theta}}\right)$
$(1 + i\cos\theta)\left(\overline{1 - 2i\cos\theta}\right) = -(1 - 2i\cos\theta)\left(\overline{1 + i\cos\theta}\right)$
$(1 + i\cos\theta)(1 + 2i\cos\theta) = -(1 - 2i\cos\theta)(1 - i\cos\theta)$
$1 + 3i\cos\theta - 2\cos^{2}\theta = -(1 - 3i\cos\theta - 2\cos^{2}\theta)$
$2 - 4\cos^{2}\theta = 0$
$\Rightarrow \cos^{2}\theta = \frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \theta = -\frac{\pi}{4}, -\frac{3\pi}{4}, \frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{3\pi}{4}, \frac{5\pi}{4}, \frac{7\pi}{4}$
sum $= 3\pi$

Let $y = y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation $\sec y \frac{dy}{dx} + 2x\sin y = x^{3}\cos y$, $y(1) = 0$. Then $y\left(\sqrt{3}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\sec^{2}y \frac{dy}{dx} + 2x\sin y \sec y = x^{3}\cos y \sec y$
$\sec^{2}y \frac{dy}{dx} + 2x\tan y = x^{3}$
$\tan y = t \Rightarrow \sec^{2}y \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{dt}{dx}$
$\frac{dt}{dx} + 2xt = x^{3}$, If $= e^{\int 2x\,dx} = e^{x^{2}}$
$te^{x^{2}} = \int x^{3} \cdot e^{x^{2}}\,dx + c$
$x^{2} = Z \Rightarrow t \cdot e^{Z} = \frac{1}{2}\int e^{Z} \cdot Z\,dZ = \frac{1}{2}\left[e^{Z} \cdot Z - e^{Z}\right] + c$
$2\tan y = (x^{2} - 1) + 2ce^{-x^{2}}$
$y(1) = 0 \Rightarrow c = 0 \Rightarrow y(\sqrt{3}) = \frac{\pi}{4}$

questions.stem: The area of the region in the first quadrant inside the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} = 8$ and outside the parabola $y^{2} = 2x$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
Required area = Ar(circle from 0 to 2) $-$ ar(para from 0 to 2)
$= \int_{0}^{2} \sqrt{8 - x^{2}}\,dx - \int_{0}^{2} \sqrt{2x}\,dx$
$= \left[\frac{x}{2}\sqrt{8 - x^{2}} + \frac{8}{2}\sin^{-1}\frac{x}{2\sqrt{2}}\right]_{0}^{2} - \sqrt{2}\left[\frac{x\sqrt{x}}{3/2}\right]_{0}^{2}$
$= \frac{2}{2}\sqrt{8 - 4} + \frac{8}{2}\sin^{-1}\frac{2}{2\sqrt{2}} - \frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}\left(2\sqrt{2} - 0\right)$
$\Rightarrow 2 + 4 \cdot \frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{8}{3} = \pi - \frac{2}{3}$

If the function $f(x) = 2x^{3} - 9ax^{2} + 12a^{2}x + 1$, $a > 0$ has a local maximum at $x = \alpha$ and a local minimum at $x = \alpha^{2}$, then $\alpha$ and $\alpha^{2}$ are the roots of the equation :
questions.solution:
$f'(x) = 6x^{2} - 18ax + 12a^{2} = 0$ (roots $\alpha$, $\alpha^{2}$)
$\alpha + \alpha^{2} = 3a$ & $\alpha \times \alpha^{2} = 2a^{2}$
$(\alpha + \alpha^{2})^{3} = 27a^{3}$
$\Rightarrow 2a^{2} + 4a^{4} + 3(3a)(2a^{2}) = 27a^{3}$
$\Rightarrow 2 + 4a^{2} + 18a = 27a$
$\Rightarrow 4a^{2} - 9a + 2 = 0$
$\Rightarrow 4a^{2} - 8a - a + 2 = 0$
$\Rightarrow (4a - 1)(a - 2) = 0 \Rightarrow a = 2$
so $6x^{2} - 36x + 48 = 0$
$\Rightarrow x^{2} - 6x + 8 = 0$ $\quad$ (1)
If we take $a = \frac{1}{4}$ then $\alpha = \frac{1}{2}$ which is not possible

$\Rightarrow 3ab - 7ba = -4ab$ always even so it is reflexive.

Case-I : odd odd

questions.stem: For $a, b > 0$, let $f(x) = \begin{cases} \dfrac{\tan((a + 1)x) + b\tan x}{x}, & x < 0 \\ 3, & x = 0 \\ \dfrac{\sqrt{ax + b^{2}x^{2}} - \sqrt{ax}}{b\sqrt{a}\,x\sqrt{x}}, & x > 0 \end{cases}$ be a continous function at $x = 0$. Then $\frac{b}{a}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$\lim_{x \to 0} f(x) = f(0) = 3$
$\lim_{x \to 0^{+}} \frac{\sqrt{ax + b^{2}x^{2}} - \sqrt{ax}}{b\sqrt{a}\,x\sqrt{x}} = 3$
$\lim_{x \to 0^{+}} \frac{ax + b^{2}x^{2} - ax}{b\sqrt{a}\,x^{3/2}\left(\sqrt{ax + b^{2}x^{2}} + \sqrt{ax}\right)}$
$\lim_{x \to 0^{+}} \frac{b^{2}}{b\sqrt{a}\left(\sqrt{a + b^{2}x} + \sqrt{a}\right)}$
$\frac{b}{\sqrt{a} \cdot 2\sqrt{a}} \Rightarrow \frac{b}{2a} = 3 \Rightarrow \frac{b}{a} = 6$

Let $a, b, c \in N$ and $a < b < c$. Let the mean, the mean deviation about the mean and the variance of the 5 observations $9, 25, a, b, c$ be $18$, $4$ and $\frac{136}{5}$, respectively. Then $2a + b - c$ is equal to _______ .
Let $\alpha|x| = |y|e^{xy - \beta}$, $\alpha, \beta \in N$ be the solution of the differential equation $x\,dy - y\,dx + xy(x\,dy + y\,dx) = 0$, $y(1) = 2$. Then $\alpha + \beta$ is equal to _
questions.solution:
$a|x| = |y|\,e^{yx - \beta}$, $a, b \in N$
$x\,dy - y\,dx + xy(x\,dy + y\,dx) = 0$
$\frac{dy}{y} - \frac{dx}{x} + (x\,dy + y\,dx) = 0$
$\ln|y| - \ln|x| + xy = c$
$y(1) = 2$
$\ln|2| - 0 + 2 = c$
$c = 2 + \ln 2$
$\ln|y| - \ln|x| + xy = 2 + \ln 2$
$\ln|x| = \ln\left|\frac{y}{2}\right| - 2 + xy$
$|x| = \left|\frac{y}{2}\right|e^{xy - 2}$
$2|x| = |y|e^{xy - 2}$
$\alpha = 2$ $\quad$ $\beta = 2$ $\quad$ $\alpha + \beta = 4$

questions.stem: If $\int \frac{1}{\sqrt[5]{(x - 1)^{4}(x + 3)^{6}}}\,dx = A\left(\frac{\alpha x - 1}{\beta x + 3}\right)^{B} + C$, where $C$ is the constant of integration, then the value of $\alpha + \beta + 20AB$ is _______ .
questions.solution:
$\int \frac{1}{\sqrt[5]{(x - 1)^{4}(x + 3)^{6}}}\,dx = A\left(\frac{\alpha x - 1}{\beta x + 3}\right)^{B} + C$
$I = \int \frac{1}{(x - 1)^{4/5}(x + 3)^{6/5}}\,dx$
$I = \int \frac{1}{\left(\frac{x - 1}{x + 3}\right)^{4/5}(x + 3)^{2}}\,dx$
$\left(\frac{x - 1}{x + 3}\right) = t \quad \Rightarrow \quad \frac{4}{(x + 3)^{2}}\,dx = dt \qquad t^{-4/5 + 1}$
$I = \frac{1}{4}\int \frac{1}{t^{4/5}}\,dt = \frac{1}{4}\,\frac{t^{1/5}}{1/5} + c$
$I = \frac{5}{4}\left(\frac{x - 1}{x + 3}\right)^{1/5} + C$
$A = \frac{5}{4}$ $\quad$ $\alpha = \beta = 1$ $\quad$ $B = \frac{1}{5}$
$\alpha + \beta + 20AB = 2 + 20 \times \frac{5}{4} \times \frac{1}{5} = 7$
